subject: VectorIQ MAP: deployment and regional lock (hosted / dedicated / private)
messages:
From: Joel Park <joel.park@vectoriq.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Initial MAP inquiry — deployment + region constraints

Vanessa,

Thanks for taking the time with our team last week. We want to formalize a mutual action plan (MAP) so both sides have clear milestones to evaluate Redwood and land a final deployment decision. High level: VectorIQ needs an LLM inference partner for customer-facing summarization workflows. Two hard constraints we flagged in discovery: EU data residency for production and an aggressive Q4 go‑live target.

Questions for the MAP:
- Can we run an evaluation PoC that represents EU traffic (latency & token costs)?
- For production, we need a path that meets our compliance — we expect Dedicated or Private to be considered. Is there a workable migration path from Hosted PoC to Dedicated/Private?

I attached the initial product requirements. Joel

Attachment: VectorIQ_requirements_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
To: Joel Park <joel.park@vectoriq.com>, Amy Chen <amy.chen@vectoriq.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-03T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Initial MAP inquiry — deployment + region constraints

Joel / Amy — thanks, this is clear and helpful. I pulled together a draft MAP for VectorIQ (attached) that outlines the PoC, evaluation criteria, and a proposed close timeline. Key points up front:

- PoC path: start with a hosted evaluation that runs EU synthetic traffic via our eu-west endpoint. This gives quick signal on latency/quality while we parallelize compliance work for a Dedicated or Private deployment.
- Production options: Hosted (fastest), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools in eu-west), Private (VPC / on-prem). For EU personal data, we generally recommend Dedicated hosted in the customer’s EU region or Redwood Private for air‑gapped requirements.
- Proposed MAP milestones:
  1) Kickoff & data access (week 0)
  2) Host PoC (2 weeks) — run vectorization + generate 5k sample sessions
  3) Compliance checklist & infra spec (parallel, 2–4 weeks)
  4) Decision checkpoint (end of week 4) — choose Hosted->Dedicated migration or Private roll-out
  5) Contract + procurement (2–3 weeks after checkpoint)

Can you confirm your internal procurement lead so we can include them on the contract/SLAs? I attached the MAP and a short SLA draft for initial redlines. We recommend planning for a staged migration: hosted PoC -> Dedicated (eu-west) -> Private only if required by legal.

Proposed next step: 30-minute working session on Mon 8/9 at 11am CET to run the MAP and lock procurement swing dates.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales (EMEA)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: VectorIQ_MAP_v1.pdf
From: Amy Chen <amy.chen@vectoriq.com>

Date: 2027-08-04T08:19:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Initial MAP inquiry — deployment + region constraints

Vanessa,

Helpful draft, thank you. A few clarifications from legal/procurement:
- EU residency is non-negotiable for production customer data. We will need either Dedicated in eu-west or Redwood Private deployed into our VPC.
- For the PoC, we can use synthetic/anonymized datasets routed to eu-west, but we need to capture audit logs and an exportable evidence package for our compliance review.
- Timeline: our procurement window is tight — if we can hit a decision checkpoint by 8/30, procurement can cut PO in early September.

Also, procurement@vectoriq.com should be on future contract threads.

Thanks,
Amy Chen
Head of IT Security, VectorIQ

Amy / Vanessa / Joel — looping in some technical detail to make the decision checkpoint more deterministic. Quick notes and a practical hybrid path: 

- Hosted PoC (eu-west): we can spin up a test tenant on our eu-west cluster. The PoC will produce trace logs and a bundle for your audit team (we'll include request/response logs, KV cache footprint, and token counts).
- Dedicated timeline: assuming legal clearance and network peering, Dedicated eu-west can be provisioned in ~3–6 weeks after PO depending on GPU profile.
- Private option: if VectorIQ requires VPC/on‑prem, plan for a longer window (6–10 weeks) and an initial discovery to scope network & KMS.

Checklist items for the MAP decision point:
- SLA targets (p50/p95 latency)
- Data residency & egress controls
- KV cache retention policy for debugging
- Rollback/fallback policy (run Hosted fallback to us-east if eu capacity constrained)

I attached the Redwood_SLA_draft.docx for procurement to review; it's intentionally conservative and we can tighten targets during redlines. Happy to jump on the 8/9 session — I can cover migration steps and a cost delta estimate between Hosted->Dedicated->Private.

—Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_SLA_draft.docx

Team — appreciate the detail and the draft MAP/SLA. VectorIQ accepts the proposed MAP and the hybrid path: start with an eu-west hosted PoC and run the compliance checklist in parallel with Dedicated provisioning. High level commitments we can sign up to for the MAP:

- Kickoff this week (8/9) and handover to engineering for data access by 8/13.
- PoC run 8/16–8/30 targeting 5k sessions and the audit evidence package.
- Decision checkpoint: 8/30 — we plan to select Dedicated eu-west if SLA and security checks pass.
- Procurement will aim to issue PO by 9/06.

Next meeting: confirm 8/10 11am CET working session for handoff and to walk the MAP. Procurement (procurement@vectoriq.com) is on copy. We'll expect the final MAP PDF and SLA redline tracker from Redwood ahead of the call.

Thanks,
Joel Park
Director of Product, VectorIQ
